reasoning: The premise that the cohort practises both kinds of return rests on E8. Its own sentence says 'now practising', but its epistemic_status is hypothetical, so the record does not establish it as fact. E4 establishes a split between counted and uncounted practice within one generation, not an uncounted generation whose members all practise both. The modal relation, may claim standing, is carried by E8, which also says Book 24 names no body that would grant it and creates none.
quote: The cohort, now practising both counted and uncounted return, may claim standing in how the valley coordinates its channel work.
alternative_reading: The claim offers no quote. Read 'uncounted generation' as the cohort and the premise stays hypothetical in E8. Read it as a wholly uncounted generation and E4 cuts against it, since practice splits within one generation.
would_settle: A record element, not hypothetical or agent-proposed, stating that the cohort as a group practises both counted and uncounted return, and naming it as the uncounted generation.
creative_room: Open: a cohort split between counted and uncounted practice may seek standing in channel coordination, and a later Book may stage that seeking. Treat as proposals, not record: the label 'uncounted generation', that each member practises both kinds, the timing 'in time', and any body that grants standing.

clauses.note: Not in the cited items. E8 names 'the cohort'; E4 says practice splits within one generation and that belief is no longer uniform, so no uniformly uncounted generation is stated.
